goldens.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH` from `protected` to `public` in `AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator`, but that only exposes the *constant*, not any new capability. Any custom authenticator could already read/set/spoof the same auth note via `context.getAuthenticationSession().getAuthNote(...)` / `setAuthNote(...)` using the literal string value. The diff doesn’t introduce new authorization checks or protections that are bypassed solely by making the constant public; it just makes the key easier to reference.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds AuthenticatorUtils.setupReauthenticationInUsernamePasswordFormError(context), a static helper that (a) reads an auth note (USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH imported from AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator, which was made public) and (b) mutates the current LoginFormsProvider via context.form().setAttribute(USERNAME_HIDDEN/REGISTRATION_DISABLED). This cross-couples a generic util class to a specific browser form authenticator’s state/behavior and to UI form attributes, and the same logic previously lived directly inside AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator.badPasswordHandler. That supports the architectural concern that this logic may fit more naturally on/near the authenticator base class rather than a generic util.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces two separate predicates that both gate “when WebAuthn/passkeys UI/data should be applied”: `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` (requires `webauthnAuth != null`, `isPasskeysEnabled()`, and `user != null`) and `WebAuthnAuthenticator.shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` (default `context.getUser() != null`, overridden to `false` in `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator`). They overlap in intent (deciding whether to prepare/show WebAuthn-related UI/data) but differ in naming, parameters, and conditions, with no shared helper. This isn’t a verifiable defect in behavior from the diff alone, but it is a concrete maintainability/architecture concern that could lead to future divergence.
